needs.reason: The four declarations are literal. Which JDK actually runs depends on the shell, not on the build: sdkman auto-env reads .sdkmanrc, jenv and some mise or asdf setups read .java-version, Maven compiles with that JDK for release 11, Gradle looks for a JDK 23 toolchain.

traps: Four files ask for four different Java versions and none overrides another: .java-version 17 (jenv, mise or asdf with idiomatic files), .sdkmanrc java=21.0.5-tem (SDKMAN), pom.xml maven.compiler.release 11 (the bytecode level javac targets, with whatever JDK runs Maven), build.gradle.kts toolchain 23 (the JDK Gradle compiles with).
21.0.5-tem is an SDKMAN candidate identifier (Temurin 21.0.5), not a plain version number; keep it as written.
The folder is two builds at once: a Maven module and a Gradle project share the same root and the same src/main/java. Each tool sees only its own file.
The Gradle build has no foojay resolver: if no JDK 23 is installed, Gradle fails to find the toolchain instead of downloading it.
There is no wrapper for either tool, so neither the Maven nor the Gradle version is declared.
Clock.java uses only Java 8 API, so it compiles at every level declared.
Neither build has modules or subprojects, so there is no workspace: two single-project builds share the folder.
